english: It is true that in some cases, significance is not meant to be attached to the particular gender used;eg, in the text "the Brāhmaṇa should not be killed" , where the prohibition is understood to apply to the killing of the female Brāhmaṇa also. But what happens in this latter case is that the direct signification of the Accusative caseending marks out the "Brāhmaṇa" to be the predominant factor by reason of his being what is most intended to be "got at" by the preadicate; and as a rule in the case of the predominant factor no significance is attached to the gender, or the number or any other factor, except what is expressed by the basic noun itself.
